description: MariaDB clusters managed by mariadb-operator, scraped with prometheus/mysqld_exporter in multi-target mode. Instances are selected through the exporter's `target` label (the MariaDB pod name) and the `job` label (the <mariadb>-metrics Service).

panels.description: Lowest `mysql_up` across the selected instances - Down means at least one instance could not be scraped by the exporter. Covers the whole MariaDB instance, not just the Instances selection.

Key server variables (from `SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES`), one row per variable per selected instance. String valued variables are not exported by mysqld_exporter and so cannot be shown here.
panels.title: Variables
Commands [$rate]
panels.description: Top 10 commands by rate (`Com_*`).

panels.title: Temporary Objects [$rate]
panels.description: A high share of on-disk temporary tables usually means `tmp_table_size` / `max_heap_table_size` are too small for the workload.

panels.title: Handlers [$rate]
panels.description: Top 10 storage engine handler operations (`Handler_*`).

panels.title: Buffer Pool Hit Ratio
panels.description: Share of buffer pool read requests served from memory. Sustained values below ~0.99 usually mean the buffer pool is too small.

panels.title: Row Lock Waits
panels.description: `Innodb_row_lock_time_avg` is reported in milliseconds.

panels.title: Redo Log
panels.description: `Innodb_log_waits` above zero means the redo log buffer is too small.

panels.title: Compression [$rate]
panels.description: Only populated for compressed tables (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INNODB_CMP).

panels.title: Replication Lag
panels.description: `Seconds_Behind_Master`. Empty on Galera-only clusters.

panels.title: Replication Threads
panels.description: 1 = running. `Slave_IO_Running=Connecting` is reported as 0.

panels.title: Master Log Position [$rate]
panels.description: Divergence between read and executed positions indicates the SQL thread is falling behind the IO thread.

panels.title: Binlog Cache [$rate]
panels.description: `Binlog_cache_disk_use` growing means `binlog_cache_size` is too small.

panels.title: Cluster Size
panels.description: `wsrep_cluster_size` as seen by each node - disagreement means a partition.

panels.title: Local State
panels.description: 1 Joining, 2 Donor/Desynced, 3 Joined, 4 Synced.

panels.title: Cluster Status / Ready
panels.description: `wsrep_cluster_status` 1 = Primary, 0 = non-Primary/Disconnected.

panels.title: Flow Control Paused
panels.description: Fraction of the interval replication was paused by flow control - the clearest sign of a slow node throttling the cluster.

panels.title: Queue Averages
panels.description: A persistently non-zero receive queue means the node cannot apply write sets as fast as it receives them.

panels.title: Certification Failures & BF Aborts [$rate]
panels.description: Write-set conflicts. Both indicate application level write contention across nodes.

panels.title: Opened Objects [$rate]
panels.description: High `Opened_tables` rate against a flat `Open_tables` suggests `table_open_cache` is too small.

namespace = "$namespace"

panels.title: Resolved Selector
panels.description: The variable values as this dashboard interpolates them into every query. The MariaDB picker shows a shortened display text, so compare the job value here against the Scrape Targets table - a stale var-mariadb in the URL, or a job label that is not <mariadb>-metrics, shows up as a mismatch here and makes every other panel empty.

Every mysqld_exporter series in the selected namespace with its full label set - deliberately filtered by namespace only. Use this to confirm the label scheme the rest of the dashboard relies on: `job` should be <mariadb>-metrics, `target` the MariaDB pod name and `role` primary/replica. mysql_up = 0 means the exporter is running but cannot query MariaDB, in which case no mysql_global_status_* metric exists at all and every other panel is empty.
panels.title: Scrape Targets
Exporter Up
panels.description: Whether the exporter could connect to each target. 0 means the exporter answered but the MariaDB probe failed - check the monitoring user's grants, TLS and the target address.

panels.title: Collector Success
panels.description: Per-collector scrape success. A collector stuck at 0 usually means the monitoring user is missing a grant or the plugin is not installed.

panels.title: Collection Duration
panels.description: Time each collector took on the last scrape.

list.description: Window for every rate()/increase() query. Must be at least twice the interval at which these series are actually stored, otherwise rate() sees a single sample per window and every graph is empty. Prefer fixing the datasource's scrape interval setting, which is what $__rate_interval is derived from.
